title: Side Lighting
description: Side lighting keys primarily from one side, around 90 degrees to the camera-subject line, so shape and texture are emphasized. Half the form goes toward light, half toward shadow.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A face or a landscape becomes sculpture. Sweat, wood grain, and cheekbones show because the light rakes.
Action and crime use it so bodies have planes; portraits use it when character should look carved. It is the wrong tool for a passport-readable hero or a beauty wrap.
Side lighting a room is not automatically split lighting. Split is the facial center-line cut with almost no wrap.
Side can still graze a shoulder, a horse, a wall.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Place the key at about 90 degrees, at a height that fits the story (eye height for a face, raking low sun for ground texture). Hardness is often hard so texture reads; soft side light exists as a large window in a side wall.
Color follows that source. Control wrap with flags if you need a truer split.
Prompt: Pure side light at 90 degrees on [Subject], half the face brilliant, half gone, texture and duality.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to carve a face or a body like sculpture, a raking desert, a sweat-lit fight. Do not use it as default coverage on a two-shot that needs both people open.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Split lighting is the hard facial version of this direction. Cross lighting uses two opposing side keys.
Kicker is a side-back accent, not a key. Short lighting and broad lighting depend on head turn relative to camera, not on 90 degrees as such.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Apocalypse Now rakes faces with hard side sources in the dark. Sicario uses raking sun and side keys so landscape and faces have grain.
The job is the 90-degree rake, not a mood.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Rembrandt (too frontal) or cross lighting (a second key). The tell is a cheek triangle, or rims on both sides.
Fix it by parking one key at 90 and killing the opposite unit.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is side lighting in film?
Light from about 90 degrees that emphasizes shape and texture. One side of the subject is bright; the other falls away.
Side lighting vs split lighting
Side lighting is the direction, usable on faces, bodies, and rooms. Split lighting is a facial pattern with a hard vertical cut and almost no wrap.
When should I use side lighting?
Use it to carve texture and duality. Skip it when both eyes must be openly keyed for a public conversation.
How do I prompt side lighting for AI image or video?
Place a single key at 90 degrees. State half the form brilliant, half gone, and name hard or soft. No second key on the far side.
